Triage first-touch: promoted to queue, type Task. The repair is a **re-measure**, not an edit: run `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` for `@objectstack/plugin-rest` against a built workspace closure, then write the tally the measurement produces — remainder listed as singletons or admitted as a gap, per the ledger's own rule. It also settles the 153-vs-`errors: 155` discrepancy the note carries on its own account. ⛔ Binding constraint from the card: do NOT adjust digits to make them sum without re-measuring — that is the exact #10722 failure mode. Size/model suggestion: S mechanical but needs the build, so M container.

---

Clause ② judged from content and not reached — a ledger data repair changes no contract accept/reject behaviour and widens no public surface.

## Zone 1 — rulings (binding)

1. ⛔ **Do not make the digits sum.** The card says this and it is the whole point: adjusting prose until it agrees with itself, with nothing re-measured, is the exact failure #10722 exists to catch. The repair is a **re-tally from tsc**.
2. **Re-measure against a built workspace closure.** `pnpm check:type-check-debt --re-measure` needs the dependency closure built first. This is proven feasible in this container — #11204's dev did it today: `turbo run build --filter=./packages/* --filter=./packages/*/*` → 70/70, then the re-measure at ~275s. Budget for it; do not skip it and reason from the ledger instead.
3. **Answer BOTH questions the note raises, not just the first.** (a) the per-code tally sums to 147 while declaring 153; (b) the note says 153 while the entry's own `errors:` field records 155. A repair that fixes the sum and leaves the 153-vs-155 discrepancy unexplained has done half the job.
4. **If the remainder cannot be attributed, admit it as a gap.** This ledger's own rule: *"an invented attribution is worse than an admitted gap."* Follow the sibling form — `plugin-approvals` writes "plus 6 singletons (TS2554 x2, TS1470, …)", `objectql` writes tiers plus singletons. Match the house spelling.
5. ⛔ Touch **only** the `@objectstack/plugin-rest` entry. #10615 is a live card on `@objectstack/plugin-auth`'s entry in the same object and is NOT yours — leave it alone, even if your re-measure shows it is also wrong. Note it in `out_of_scope_findings` instead.

## Zone 2 — mechanism assumptions to falsify before you rely on them

- ⚠️ **The card's arithmetic is the card's, not a measurement.** 67+57+13+10 = 147 is checkable from the ledger text, but whether 147/153/155 is the *current* truth is not — the note is dated and the tree has moved. Re-derive all three numbers before deciding which one is wrong. It is entirely possible that none of them matches today's tsc and the repair is a full re-tally rather than a remainder clause.
- **`errors: 155` is a ceiling this gate enforces.** Before you touch it, establish whether your re-measured number is above or below it — the gate is shrink-only, and a number that moves the wrong way is a red `main`, not a data repair. If tsc now reports *more* than 155, STOP and report: that is a regression card, not this card.
- **"the tally was taken at 153" may describe a different measurement basis** than `errors:` — e.g. one counted before a NodeNext pass, or one counting files rather than diagnostics. Read the surrounding ledger prose and the sibling entries before assuming the two numbers were ever meant to agree.
- ⚠️ A re-measure that reports **0** for this package would be a graduation, not a tally repair — and a zero-hit reading needs a positive control before you believe it (a misconfigured invocation reports 0 too). #11204's dev has a worked example of that control on the card.

## Zone 3 — suggested routes (not binding)

- The two sibling entries named in the card (`plugin-approvals`, `objectql`) are the format precedent; copying their shape is cheaper than inventing one.
- If the re-measure is expensive to repeat, capture the per-code histogram once and derive every number in the note from that single run, so the note's parts cannot disagree with each other again.
- #10722's docblock uses this very entry as its worked example for why summing per-code tallies would red an accurate entry — read it before changing anything about how tallies are written, and do not change that rule here.

**ACCEPT** — PR #11496, head `9fef66af`.

## The card's title names a package that does not exist — and my claim comment repeated it

Verified independently, with a live positive control: a sweep of every `package.json` on `origin/main` finds **no** `@objectstack/plugin-rest`, while the same sweep finds `@objectstack/rest` in `packages/rest/package.json`. The ledger keys the entry `'@objectstack/rest'` at `:844`.

So the card's title, and my Zone 1 which wrote `TEST_DEBT['@objectstack/plugin-rest']` straight from it, both named something that isn't in the repo. The dev traced the mis-naming to the **COMPOSITION docblock** — which is the same place the stale tally was being cited from. The wrong name and the wrong number came out of the same sentence.

## The proof that no digit was fudged is the strongest part

Ruling 1 was "do not make the digits sum", and the evidence that they didn't is not an assurance — it is the shape of the movement:

| class | old note | re-measured |
|:---|---:|---:|
| TS2835 | 67 | **72** ↑ |
| TS7006 | 57 | **49** ↓ |
| TS2550 | 10 | **16** ↑ |
| TS2554 | 13 | **14** ↑ |
| singletons | *(none named)* | 4 (TS2769 ×2, TS2345, TS6133) |

The old shape moved in **both directions**, and two classes it never named are in the pile. **No rescale of the old numbers could have produced this** — which is precisely what distinguishes a re-measure from a repair-by-arithmetic. Total: 155, exactly the recorded field.

## Both questions answered, and the second answer is better than the one I asked for

Ruling 3 asked for the 153-vs-155 discrepancy to be explained rather than left. The answer is not "someone miscounted": **153 was measured at `e8db1a230`, and `errors` was later lowered onto a *different* measurement (155 at `55da611`, #6939) without the composition being re-taken across that move.** The note's own "not re-tallied by class at the 155 below" clause was saying exactly this, and nobody had read it as a pointer. The two numbers were never one measurement disagreeing with itself.

The 6 unaccounted at 153 are retired **unattributed** — the per-class breakdown at `e8db1a230` was never retained, and this ledger's rule is that an invented attribution is worse than an admitted gap. Correct call.

`errors: 155` is **unchanged** — not above the shrink-only ceiling (no regression card), not below it (no lowering, no graduation). A note-only change that moves no ratchet in either direction.

## The instrumentation was handled correctly

Getting the histogram required temporarily instrumenting the gate itself — a measurement that mutates its own instrument. It was restored **byte-identically before the real edit was written**: sha256 `5a795e74…` before and after, `git diff --quiet` exit 0, `grep -c __DUMP_LABEL` → 0. No instrumentation reaches the diff. That is the difference between borrowing an instrument and contaminating it.

Positive control for the reading: 155, not 0; spread over 64 named test files; and it independently equals a number a different party recorded at a different commit. A misconfigured invocation does not produce that coincidence.

## The scope call — accepted, and it was the right one

You flagged honestly that editing the COMPOSITION docblock strains my ruling 5, and invited me to split it out. I'm accepting it, because ruling 5 was about **other packages' ledger entries** — #10615's `plugin-auth` entry is the thing it was protecting, and that is untouched. The docblock is not another card's entry; it is a statement **your own edit falsified**.

Leaving it would have been worse, and specifically so: that docblock's job is to stop someone "fixing" the rule into summing per-code tallies, using this entry as the worked example of why summing would red an accurate entry. Re-tallied, the example now sums to exactly `errors` — so a reader who checks it finds the example refuting itself and concludes the *rule* is wrong. Marking the example retired while leaving the rule untouched is the minimal edit that keeps the file honest.

This lane has now hit that same class three times in two rounds — #11476 (a `rootDir` comment denying the declaration below it), #10901 (a scan whose comment-era assumptions drifted from its callers), and this. Stale knowledge sitting next to correct machinery is this repo's most common defect shape.

## Out-of-scope handling

- **#11497** filed: two untracked surpluses (`plugin-approvals` 348/347, `runtime` 227/226) whose named class tracker **#6376 is closed**, so nothing open tracks them.
- **#10615 drift, deliberately NOT filed as new**: that card was written at "records 109 where tsc now reports 98"; today's re-measure reports **97**, so its surplus has widened 11 → 12. Recording it rather than filing a duplicate, and rather than letting the card's number be read as current, is exactly right.

## CI

By latest run per name: 31 runs, **0 failure, 0 cancelled**. The decisive gate is green — **`Type Check · debt ledger` success**, which runs `check:type-check-debt` (`--self-test` *and* `--re-measure`), so both the structural half and the measurement agree in CI and not only on your machine. Landing once `Lint & Repo Gates` reports.

Verification will be by **content on `origin/main`**, with a positive control.

`errors: 155` unchanged — no ratchet moved in either direction.

**Positive control** (this is the part that makes the reading mean anything): four sibling entries still match their own patterns — `plugin-security`, `formula`, `verify`, `connector-mcp` each = 1. So the grep works and only this entry changed.

## One thing I expected wrong, and checking it was worth it

I predicted `counted at 153` would be gone. It appears **twice**, and both are correct:

- `:855` — inside the entry's own `WHAT THIS REPLACES` section, quoting the old tally verbatim **as history** before showing why no rescale could have produced the new numbers. This is the ledger's house pattern, and the gate knows it: its docblock says a phrase appearing *"later in the note means the note is quoting its own history and the entry is skipped."*
- `:1733` — the COMPOSITION docblock, which now marks the worked example **retired** while re-arguing the rule it illustrates: *"changes nothing about the rule: a tally that happens to be complete today is still not one a gate may REQUIRE to be complete, and the next deliberately partial tally must stay writable."*

That is the scope expansion I accepted, executed exactly as reasoned — the example is retired because your own edit falsified it, and the rule it protects is left standing and restated. Had you not touched it, the docblock would have been citing an example that now refutes itself, and the next reader would have had grounds to delete the rule.
